DronG/Getty Images We all know that leaving food out for too long can be risky. But what happens when food isn't kept at the right temperature before it even reaches your kitchen?
 That's the exact concern behind a new recall involving two refrigerated pasta products sold at ALDI stores in four states.
 On November 16, ALDI announced a recall of Priano Protein Carbonara Tortelloni and Priano Protein Herb & Cheese Tortelloni found at select stores because "the products may not have been stored, distributed, or sold at appropriate temperatures, which may allow growth of pathogens including Clostridium botulinum ," a bacterium that can multiply in food stored at temperatures that are too warm.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Adds the ALDI post, "Consumers are warned not to prepare or consume the affected products from the impacted states, even if they do not look or smell spoiled."
 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) also published the company announcement on November 17.
 What to know about botulism
 Eating foods contaminated with Clostridium botulinum can cause botulism, which the Cleveland Clinic explains is a rare but serious illness that disrupts your body's nervous system. If left untreated, botulism can lead to life-threatening complications and even death.
 Some of the most common symptoms of botulism include abdominal pain or discomfort, general weakness, dizziness, double vision, a swollen belly, and trouble speaking or swallowing. Consumers experiencing these problems should seek immediate medical attention.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement To date, no illnesses have been reported in connection to the current recall.
 How to check for the recalled tortellini
 The affected tortellini products were available for purchase in stores and online in Alabama, Georgia, North Carolina, and South Carolina. According to the company website , Priano is an ALDI-exclusive brand.
 The recall notice provides the following details:
 Priano Protein Carbonara Tortelloni (9 oz.) 
 Lot number: T9101926
 Best-if-used-by date: 12/18/2026
 Priano Protein Herb & Cheese Tortelloni (9 oz.) 
 Lot number: T9101926
 Best-if-used-by date: 12/18/2026
 According to the product photos in the recall notice, both products are packaged in clear plastic containers: the Priano Protein Carbonara tortellini has a purple label, while the Priano Protein Herb & Cheese has a green label.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement In a statement, ALDI says it "immediately took action to remove impacted product from store shelves" once the issue was discovered. The company urges consumers who have purchased the affected tortellini to discard the products immediately—even if they look or smell normal—or return them to their local ALDI store for a full refund.
